authorities.proposition: The courts of appeals have jurisdiction over interlocutory district-court orders granting, continuing, modifying, refusing, or dissolving injunctions, or refusing to dissolve or modify injunctions.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 8(a); 4th Cir. R. 8
authorities.proposition: A party ordinarily must first seek a stay or injunction from the district court; a circuit motion must show that district-court relief would be impracticable or state that relief was sought and denied with the district court's reasons, and must include supporting record materials and sworn facts when disputed.

authorities.citation: Billups v. City of Charleston, 961 F.3d 673 (4th Cir. 2020)
authorities.proposition: Paid tour-guide speech is protected by the First Amendment, and a licensing requirement that burdens protected expression in public streets and sidewalks is subject to constitutional scrutiny even when framed as an occupational rule.

authorities.citation: Billups v. City of Charleston, 961 F.3d 673 (4th Cir. 2020)
authorities.proposition: For a content-neutral speech restriction, the government bears the burden to establish narrow tailoring with evidence connecting the chosen burden to its asserted interests and accounting for substantially less restrictive alternatives.

A preliminary-injunction movant must clearly establish each Winter factor; legal conclusions are reviewed de novo, factual findings for clear error, and the ultimate preliminary-injunction decision for abuse of discretion.

Rules 65(c) and 65(d) require an express security determination and an injunction stated in reasonably specific terms; corrective remand may leave warranted interim protection in force until the district court enters a superseding compliant order.

A stay is discretionary relief governed by likelihood of success, irreparable injury to the movant, substantial injury to other parties, and the public interest; the first two factors are the most critical.

authorities.citation: Robinson v. National Collegiate Athletic Ass'n, No. 25-2003 (4th Cir. Apr. 3, 2026)
authorities.proposition: Expiration of one short recurring event does not necessarily moot a dispute where the challenged rule remains operative and the same party is reasonably expected to face the same time-limited controversy again.
